text:

Read the syllabus and ensure you understand the course procedures and grading.
Download the install the latest versions of R and RStudio. R must be installed first so that RStudio can use it.

R (Mac OS X | Windows
RStudio (Mac OS X | Windows)

Fix your settings in RStudio to use the code diagnostics.
IMPORTANT: Create a GitHub account
IMPORTANT Post your GitHub username on the GitHub Usernames google sheet. After roughly 10 minutes (during normal working hours), you should receive two emails. One email will be an invitation from “GitHub” to join the BYUI335 organization. Accept the invitation. The other email will be an invitation from “Katie Allen” to collaborate on a repository with your name on it. Accept the invitation. If you do not see the two emails, check your spam folder.

Normally you would create your own repository, but because we want your class repository saved in a special organization we are creating it for you. You will be using this repository to turn in assignments.

Join the Data Science Society workspace in Slack. This is where we will have class conversations and ask questions. Here is the link to join: https://join.slack.com/t/byuidss/signup . The following sub-bullets provide additional detailed instructions about setting up and using slack.

Create a professional username, something you could share with an employer
In addition to the channels you are automatically add to, be sure to join the following two channels:

Our class channel. It will look something like #ds350_s22_allen or #ds350_s22_woodruff. Find the appropriate channel and add yourself to it. Once you are in the class channel, introduce yourself by replying to the introduction thread by clicking the thread, hit reply, then type a brief introduction.
#tutoring_lab, add this channel. It is where you can ask questions about code related to specific tasks or case studies.
Browse through the channels and join as as many as you are interested in. This community will be a great resource, even if you are not a Data Science major.

Extra features are available when you install Slack as an app on your PC and/or phone. The more comfortable you become with using Slack, the easier it will be to collaborate with each other throughout your professional career.

Post a professional picture to your GitHub, LinkedIn, and Slack icons. Go to the BYU-Idaho LinkedIn Photobooth if you don’t have a professional picture.
Make plans to attend Data Science Society on the second Wednesday of the semester.
Download the R script first-R-script.R and open it in RStudio. Run each line of code, one at a time (figure out the keyboard shortcut to do this). Note any questions you want to ask your group when you get to class.

It is not crucial that you understand what each line of code does at this point in the semester. However, briefly try guessing what each line of code does before running it, but don’t worry if you don’t understand all (or any of) the code.




Git is a program that helps you organize code and keep track of any changes you make. Git uses folders called “repositories” to organize code into different projects. GitHub is an online platform where you can store your Git repositories, and then access them from any computer. You will use Git and GitHub this semester to submit your homework, in a repository made specifically for this class.

Study Chapter 8: R for Data Science—Projects
Install Git on your computer. Then link the repository we created for you on GitHub to an RStudio project dedicated specifically to this class. Either read these instructions or watch this video that walks you through the process of setting everything up and ensuring RStudio is talking to GitHub. If you can’t get it to work, reach out for help! This is a critical step to being able to turn in assignments.






Warning



If you didn’t put your Github info on the google sheet referenced in the “pre” part of this task, and accept the two invitations, then you will need to do so ASAP. Do not simply create your own repository since we want the repository to belong to our class organization.


After completing step 2 above , edit the README.md in RStudio to include a short description of yourself, and “push” the changes to the online version of your repository.
To practice “pulling”:

Now edit your README.md file from online instead of from within RStudio. Navigate to your repository and open the readme.md file. Below your description, add links to the repos of everyone in your group (you may need to finish this part in class, or ask them over slack).
Go back to RStudio. Notice that the repo links do not appear in your README.md
Using the terminal (next to the console) or Git tab in RStudio, pull the online changes you made to update the files on your hard drive.
Let’s make one more change to README.md in RStudio by adding the name of your group. Then push the change to GitHub online.


You will want to get in the habit of pull, add/stage, commit, push (in that order!) at least once everyday.


Once you have completed all that you can for the week, include a link to the readme.md file in the Week 1 Submission on I-learn. Don’t submit multiple times to the submission box in I-learn, just submit 1 time at the end of the week and include all the links to what you want graded that week.

title: 3  Great British Bake Off
text:
ResourcesBackgroundPrePost




Chapter 10: Tibbles




data structures
The previous guided instruction could still be helpful if you have not yet completed it: data wrangling with dplyr




The Great British Bake Off was a hit reality TV show that put amateur bakers against each other. Contestants were eliminated in each round until a winner was crowned. The show ran for 12 seasons (a season is called a series in the dataset) through 2021, with plenty of drama. You will analyze the show’s 7-day viewership (i.e. TV ratings over a 7 day period).
Specifically, you want to know how the 7-day viewership changes within a season and across seasons. In one graph, you compare the 7-day viewership for the season’s premiere and finale. In another graph, you compare the mean across seasons while not losing track of each episode’s 7-day viewership.
